steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a large mixing bowl beat butter until soft, add sugar, and beat until fluffy. Add egg and vanilla, beat well.

In a medium bowl stir together flour, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt. With mixer on low speed, gradually add four mixture to butter mixture, beat until well mixed. With a wooden spoon, stir in oats, zucchini, walnuts or pecans, chocolate and butterscotch pieces.
Drop by rounded teaspoons about 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake for 10-12 minutes or until golden brown. Cool sheets and then cookies on a cooling rack. ENJOY!

raw_recipe.headline: Martian Cookies
raw_recipe.description: I think these are called martian cookies because of the green flecks, and they are out of this world!

review.reviewBody: For a healthy cookie these hit the spot. I used brown sugar instead of white and cut it down to 1/2 cup. Also I used all whole wheat flour. The butterscotch chips make these phenomenal and so you don't miss the sugar. Thanks for a way to use up all the zucchini I've got in my freezer!

Amazing Cookies! I drained my zucchini a colander- a weighed bowl on top to remove the excess water. I also use all chocolate chips, my family doesn't care for butterscotch. Lastly you can substitute butter flavor crisco for real butter. I needed to in a pinch...it worked.

My son and I made these. We tripled the recipe and added an additional 1 1/2 cups of chocolate chips but did not use the nuts or butterscotch chips. My boys say they are 5 star. I gave them a four only because they are a "little" bland. I think they need frosting, but my boys say they are perfect without it. They are definitely a cake cookie. Not flat our crispy. We decided they should be cooked at 375 for 12 minutes. Otherwise they take 16 minutes and dry out some. 

Thanks for a nice healthy cookie recipe!

These cookies are amazing! I made them last year for a family reunion and they have been requested many times since then. So moist and cake-like--delicious! I pressed out the moisture in the zucchini before adding to the batter to make sure it didn't get too wet. Great way to use up zucchini other than in zucchini bread!

I can't believe how fast these cookies go - each person that I introduce to them falls in love. I work with 2 dieticians who even give their approval! I shred zukes and freeze them for the winter to add nutrition, bulk and fiber to various foods - the one downfall of that is that it is a little soggy when it unfreezes. (2cups frozen=1cup 'squeezed out' That is actually a benefit for these cookies since the dough is very thick until you add the zucchini. It also makes for the perfect cookie texture: thick, full of ingredients (these cookies definitely aren't the type to cook out flat), cake-like but firm enough to give you a great bite without falling apart. Yum, Yum, YUM!!! Not one person has disagreed. They're my new potluck staple and it's so exciting to discuss - yes you CAN make desserts more healthy. Most definitely thanks for sharing this recipe! And I LOVE the name 'Martian cookies' - that sells the kids everytime, not to mention great for St. Patty's Day too :-)

Delicious! Great way to get your family eating more veggies :) I did replace the white sugar with brown and reduced the amount of sugar down to 1/2 cup.Butterscotch chips were delicious with the chocolate and zucchini, plus the oatmeal gave the cookies another health kick plus were nice and moist. Will definetly make again! Highly recommend.

I just made these cookies, they are good. I substituted coconut oil for the butter. I also did change a few other things with what I had and did not have on hand. No choco chips, used craisons. I also didn't use the nuts. I added 1/2c coconut flakes. They are soft and just so good. Will definetly make these cookies again.

These are a very soft/cake like cookie, but still tasty. Next time I make them I am going to try omitting the choc chips and double the butterscotch chips instead. I used frozen shredded zucchini that I had left over from last season. It worked really well.

Very interesting. Taste is good, but different--a conglomerate collection of cookies! I found 12 minutes was enough. Used 1/2 brown sugar and 1/4 white sugar. Rolled into balls-they held their shape well.

The only changes I made to the original were to use 1/2 butter and 1/2 applesauce and I omitted the nuts. They took longer than the 12min the recipe stated to cook. The flavor was good, though. Good base cookie recipe. I think next time I'm going to try baking them at 375 like some of the other reviews suggest. Plan to also use 1/4c mini chocolate chips and 1/4 cup mini mms.

I subbed blueberry cruising for the choc chips. They’re not too sweet, which I like. Had to pat these down when they were done cooking to flatten out a bit, and needed 15 minutes to get the bottom golden brown. The tops never really darken so don’t be fooled! Great recipe!
My family loves these. So tasty. I’ve had these years ago when I was a kid.
Very good . Have used peanut butter chips in place of butterscotch and that works well too
They are okay but weren't a hit here. I like all of the ingredients, however maybe too much going on and not enough flavor in the batter itself. Won't be making again.
Delicious! Zucchini makes up for the extra butter in other oatmeal cookies. I look forward to making these again.
Fun cookies! Ours spread quite a bit but I think our zucchini was exceptionally watery. Still a great tasting cookie.
WIll make again! I substituted purée pumpkin for the zucchini, they were a family favourite with all the mix-ins!

Made them per recipe-no substations. I took them as a donation for volunteers at a non profit. People started asking who made them, then finding me to tell me how good they are! When I make them again, I will double the recipe! Thank you Allrecipes.com!
We loved them. Made no changes to the recipe, super moist and chewy. Making these for visiting family soon.
Made it exactly according to recipe. Very good and moist cookies. Freeze well too. Good use for all that zucchini in the garden.
